## 1. System Vision & Operational Problem
### 1.1 Target User & The High-Stakes Problem
**The User:** A Senior Documentary Credit Examiner at an Issuing Bank examining incoming export presentations under irrevocable Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700) and amendments (MT707).
When a presentation (Commercial Invoice, Ocean Bill of Lading, Packing List, Insurance Policy/Certificate, Certificate of Origin) arrives at the bank's counter, the examiner is governed by **ICC UCP 600** and **ISBP 745**. They face three operational traps that neither rigid rule engines nor naive RAG/LLM pipelines handle reliably:
1. **The 5-Banking-Day Preclusion Cliff (UCP 600 Art. 14(b) & Art. 16):** - Under **Art. 14(b)**, the examining bank has a maximum of **5 banking days** following the day of presentation to determine whether a presentation is complying. - If the bank decides to refuse, it must issue a **single Notice of Refusal (SWIFT MT734)** under **Art. 16(c)** stating *all* discrepancies and the exact disposition of documents under **Art. 16(c)(iii)**. - Under **Art. 16(f)**, if the bank fails to act within 5 banking days or fails to state a valid discrepancy in that single notice, it is **legally precluded** from claiming the documents do not constitute a complying presentation ($100K–$10M+ balance-sheet exposure).
2. **The Wrongful Dishonor vs. Genuine Discrepancy Trap (UCP 600 Art. 14(d), 14(e), 14(j), Art. 18(c) & ISBP 745 Para A23):** - Naive regex/rule checks flag harmless typographical errors (e.g., `"Industrial AC Servo Mashine"` instead of `"Industrial AC Servo Machine"`). Under **ISBP 745 Para A23**, a misspelling or typing error that does not affect the meaning of the word or the sentence in which it occurs does *not* make a document discrepant. Refusing payment on this basis exposes the bank to **wrongful dishonor** litigation. - Under **UCP 600 Art. 14(e)**, in documents *other than* the commercial invoice, the description of the goods may be in general terms not conflicting with their description in the credit (e.g., `"Industrial Servo Motors"` on the Bill of Lading vs. the full model specification on the Commercial Invoice under **Art. 18(c)**). - Conversely, under **UCP 600 Art. 14(j)**, while addresses of the beneficiary and applicant need not be the same as those stated in the credit, when the applicant's address appears as part of the *Consignee* or *Notify Party* details on a transport document, it **must be the same as that stated in the credit**.
3. **Stateful Amendment Ambiguity (UCP 600 Art. 10(c) & 10(e)) & Cross-Silo Blindness:** - Under **Art. 10(c)**, the terms and conditions of the original credit remain in force for the beneficiary until the beneficiary communicates its acceptance of the amendment, or presents documents that comply with the credit and with the not-yet-accepted amendment. Under **Art. 10(e)**, partial acceptance of an amendment is not allowed and will be deemed a notification of rejection. Standard RAG dumps both original terms and unaccepted amendments into the context window, causing LLMs to enforce unaccepted terms. - Finally, documentary compliance is distinct from **Financial Crime / Sanctions / TBML compliance**. A presentation may be 100% compliant on its face under UCP 600 (Art. 4 & Art. 5 separate documents from goods/underlying fraud), yet exhibit severe **Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML)** unit-price inflation or a sanctioned parent entity—requiring an immediate **Compliance Hold & AML Escalation** rather than a standard UCP 600 documentary refusal.

## 3. Core Technical Differentiation (The 3 Pillars)
### Pillar 1: Strict Neuro-Symbolic Split (Hard Invariant Rule)
LLMs should never do calendar math or percentage tolerances; rule engines should never judge semantic typos. VERITAS-600 enforces a **Hard Invariant Rule**: *A neural LLM verdict can never override a failed deterministic check.*
1. **Deterministic Symbolic Engine (`ucp600_deterministic.py`):** - **Temporal checks:** Presentation date $\le$ Expiry date (**Art. 6(d)(i)**); Presentation date $\le$ Shipment date $+ 21\text{ calendar days}$ (**Art. 14(c)**); On-board date $\le$ Effective latest shipment date (**Art. 20(a)(ii)**); 5-banking-day examination clock (**Art. 14(b)**). - **Financial & quantity math:** Invoice amount $\le$ Available LC credit amount (**Art. 18(b)**); Currency identity check (**Art. 18(a)(iii)** & **Art. 28(f)(i)**); Quantity tolerance within $\pm 5\%$ where permitted (**Art. 30(b)**). - **Insurance coverage & document type (Art. 28(c), 28(e) & 28(f)(ii)):** - **Art. 28(c):** Rejects `Cover Notes` (must be an Insurance Policy or Insurance Certificate under an open cover). - **Art. 28(e):** $\text{InsuranceEffectiveDate} \le \text{ShipmentDate}$ (unless it explicitly states cover is effective from a date not later than the date of shipment). - **Art. 28(f)(ii):** Minimum insured amount must be at least $110\%$ of the CIF or CIP value of the goods (or, if CIF/CIP cannot be determined from the documents, $110\%$ of the greater of the amount for which honor/negotiation is requested or the gross value of the goods shown on the commercial invoice): $$\text{InsuredValue} \ge 1.10 \times \max(\text{CIF\_CIP\_Value},\ \text{RequestedDrawingAmount},\ \text{InvoiceGrossValue})$$ - **Cross-document physical reconciliation (Art. 14(d)):** Net and gross weight consistency across Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and Bill of Lading (data in a document must not conflict with data in any other stipulated document).
2. **Neural Legal Adjudication Engine (`ucp600_legal_adjudicator.py`):** - Invoked *only* on semantic/lexical divergences between documents. - Evaluates whether a divergence is: - **Protected under ISBP 745 Para A23:** A misspelling or typing error that does not affect the meaning of the word or the sentence in which it occurs (e.g., `"Industrial AC Servo Mashine"`). - **Protected under UCP 600 Art. 14(e):** A general goods description on a non-invoice document (e.g., `"Industrial Servo Motors"` on the Bill of Lading vs. `"Industrial AC Servo Machine Model X-200"` on the Commercial Invoice) that does not conflict with the LC description. - **A Material Discrepancy under Art. 18(c) or Art. 14(j):** A conflicting or omitted specification on the Commercial Invoice (**Art. 18(c)**), or a mutated applicant address inside the Consignee/Notify Party box of a transport document (**Art. 14(j)**).
### Pillar 2: Stateful Amendment Memory (Art. 10(c) & 10(e) Quarantine)
Before running any check, `amendment_memory.py` builds an **Active Term Snapshot** and an **Audit Lineage Graph**: - If Amendment #1 (`latest_shipment_date` extended from Oct 10 to Oct 18) is marked `ACCEPTED`, the active state updates to Oct 18. - If Amendment #2 (`port_of_discharge` changed and `unit_price` reduced) is `UNACCEPTED_PENDING`, the memory engine evaluates whether the beneficiary's presented documents conform to *all* changes in Amendment #2 (implicit acceptance under Art. 10(c)) or adhere strictly to the pre-Amendment #2 state. Under **Art. 10(e)**, partial adherence to an amendment is flagged as a rejection/discrepancy.
### Pillar 3: Cross-Silo Risk & Bank-Officer Action Engine (With Human-in-the-Loop Gate)
1. **Zetaris Federated Risk Check:** Joins the active LC against `parquet_customs` to compute the HS-code unit price $Z$-score: $$Z = \frac{\text{InvoiceUnitPrice} - \mu_{\text{HS6}}}{\sigma_{\text{HS6}}}$$ and checks all presentation parties and the carrying vessel IMO against `opensanctions_entities` (including parent company ownership). 2. **Bank-Officer Action Engine (`decision_engine.py`):** Produces one of three bank-side actions—always gated by a **"Human Examiner Approve & Sign"** button before finalizing: - **Action 1 — Honor / Approve Settlement:** All UCP 600 deterministic and neural checks pass, and Sanctions/TBML checks are clear (even if harmless ISBP 745 Para A23 typos exist). - **Action 2 — Issue MT734 Notice of Refusal with Cure/Waiver Advisory (Art. 16(c)(iii)(a) or (b)):** Documentary discrepancies exist (e.g., Art. 28(f)(ii) insurance at $108\%$ and Art. 14(d) weight conflict), Sanctions Risk $= 0$, and 11 days remain in the 21-day presentation window. The bank issues a formal SWIFT MT734 stating all discrepancies, holds the documents under **Art. 16(c)(iii)(a)/(b)**, and attaches a **Pre-Expiry Re-Presentation / Applicant Waiver Cost Comparison** showing that beneficiary re-presentation of corrected insurance/packing documents within 48 hours saves $\$11,100$ in port demurrage compared to a 6-day applicant waiver cycle. - **Action 3 — Compliance Hold & AML/Sanctions Escalation (Non-MT734 Freeze):** When documents comply on their face under UCP 600, but Zetaris detects a severe TBML price anomaly ($Z > 4.0$) or an OFAC/OpenSanctions parent-entity hit. Because sanctions/TBML are regulatory blocks rather than UCP 600 documentary discrepancies, the system **blocks settlement**, places a **Compliance Hold**, and generates a **Financial Crime Escalation Dossier (SAR/OFAC Hold)** rather than an invalid MT734 documentary refusal.

## 6. Database & Join-Safe Federated Query Specifications
### 6.1 PostgreSQL Schema (`apps/api/db/schema.sql`)
```sql CREATE TABLE lc_master ( lc_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, swift_mt700_raw TEXT NOT NULL, issuing_bank VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, applicant_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, applicant_address_strict VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL, beneficiary_name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, currency VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD', amount NUMERIC(15, 2) NOT NULL, tolerance_pct NUMERIC(5, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.00, incoterm VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, hs_code_6 VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL, goods_description_strict TEXT NOT NULL, unit_price NUMERIC(12, 2) NOT NULL, quantity INTEGER NOT NULL, port_of_loading VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, port_of_discharge VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL, latest_shipment_date DATE NOT NULL, expiry_date DATE NOT NULL, presentation_period_days INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 21, insurance_min_pct NUMERIC(6, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 110.00, -- UCP 600 Art. 28(f)(ii) daily_demurrage_usd NUMERIC(10, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1850.00 );
CREATE TABLE lc_amendments ( amendment_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, lc_id VARCHAR(32) REFERENCES lc_master(lc_id), sequence_no INTEGER NOT NULL, amended_field VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, old_value TEXT NOT NULL, new_value TEXT NOT NULL, beneficiary_acceptance_status VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL CHECK ( beneficiary_acceptance_status IN ('ACCEPTED', 'REJECTED', 'UNACCEPTED_PENDING') ), effective_date DATE NOT NULL );
CREATE TABLE examination_audit_log ( run_id VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY, lc_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, executed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), active_terms_sha256 VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, zetaris_execution_mode VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, -- 'LIVE_ZETARIS' or 'LOCAL_DUCKDB_FALLBACK' zetaris_query_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, deterministic_result JSONB NOT NULL, neural_adjudication_result JSONB NOT NULL, recommended_action VARCHAR(48) NOT NULL, -- 'APPROVE_HONOUR', 'ISSUE_MT734_REFUSAL', 'COMPLIANCE_HOLD_AML' human_approved_by VARCHAR(128) NULL, human_approved_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL, generated_artifact_text TEXT NULL ); ```
### 6.2 Join-Safe Zetaris 3-Silo Federated Query (`apps/api/zetaris/sql/federated_check.sql`)
To prevent row multiplication when an LC has multiple amendments or multiple watchlist matches, amendments and sanctions hits are pre-aggregated in CTEs before joining to `lc_master`. This guarantees **exactly 1 row per `lc_id`**.
```sql WITH accepted_shipment_amd AS ( SELECT lc_id, new_value AS effective_shipment_date FROM postgres_trade.lc_amendments WHERE amended_field = 'latest_shipment_date' AND beneficiary_acceptance_status = 'ACCEPTED' ORDER BY sequence_no DESC LIMIT 1 ), unaccepted_amendments_agg AS ( SELECT lc_id, COUNT(*) AS quarantined_count, STRING_AGG(amended_field || '=' || new_value, '; ') AS quarantined_amendments_summary FROM postgres_trade.lc_amendments WHERE beneficiary_acceptance_status = 'UNACCEPTED_PENDING' GROUP BY lc_id ), sanctions_hits_agg AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS hit_count, MAX(risk_score) AS max_risk_score, STRING_AGG( matched_name || ' (Parent: ' || COALESCE(parent_company_name, 'N/A') || ' | ' || sanction_program || ')', '; ' ) AS sanctions_summary FROM opensanctions_entities.watchlist WHERE lookup_name IN (:beneficiary_name, :vessel_name, :notify_party_name) ) SELECT lc.lc_id, lc.applicant_name, lc.beneficiary_name, lc.amount AS lc_amount, lc.unit_price AS lc_unit_price, lc.latest_shipment_date AS original_shipment_date, COALESCE(amd_acc.effective_shipment_date, CAST(lc.latest_shipment_date AS VARCHAR)) AS effective_shipment_date, COALESCE(amd_unacc.quarantined_count, 0) AS quarantined_amendment_count, amd_unacc.quarantined_amendments_summary, -- Silo 2: Parquet Customs HS-Code Unit Price Benchmark cust.hs_code_6, cust.description AS hs_description, cust.mean_unit_price_usd, cust.stddev_unit_price_usd, ROUND((:invoice_unit_price - cust.mean_unit_price_usd) / NULLIF(cust.stddev_unit_price_usd, 0), 2) AS tbml_price_zscore, -- Silo 3: Aggregated OpenSanctions Watchlist Hits COALESCE(sanc.hit_count, 0) AS sanction_hit_count, COALESCE(sanc.max_risk_score, 0.0) AS sanction_max_risk_score, sanc.sanctions_summary FROM postgres_trade.lc_master lc LEFT JOIN accepted_shipment_amd amd_acc ON lc.lc_id = amd_acc.lc_id LEFT JOIN unaccepted_amendments_agg amd_unacc ON lc.lc_id = amd_unacc.lc_id LEFT JOIN parquet_customs.hs_benchmarks cust ON lc.hs_code_6 = cust.hs_code_6 CROSS JOIN sanctions_hits_agg sanc WHERE lc.lc_id = :lc_id; ```

## 🏛️ Executive Summary
In global trade finance, **Letters of Credit (LCs)** govern billions of dollars daily under **ICC UCP 600** and **ISBP 745**. When shipping documents arrive, bank documentary credit examiners face high-stakes operational traps:
1. **The 5-Banking-Day Preclusion Cliff (UCP 600 Art. 14(b) & Art. 16):** Banks have only 5 banking days to audit documents. Failing to state all valid discrepancies in a single **SWIFT MT734 Notice of Refusal** legally precludes the bank from refusing payment ($100K–$10M+ balance-sheet loss). 2. **The Wrongful Dishonor Trap:** Rigid regex checks reject harmless typos (e.g., `"Industrial AC Servo Mashine"`). Under **ISBP 745 Para A23**, non-meaning-altering misspellings are legally protected. Wrongful refusals trigger massive litigation. 3. **Stateful Amendment Ambiguity & Cross-Silo TBML:** Standard LLMs confuse original terms with unaccepted amendments (**Art. 10(c)/(e)**). Furthermore, documents may look 100% compliant on paper while hiding **Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML)** unit-price inflation ($Z > +5.0$) or sanctioned parent companies—requiring a **Regulatory AML Freeze**, not a documentary refusal.
**VERITAS-600** solves this with a production-grade **Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Architecture**, combining deterministic Python math engines, stateful amendment memory, in-situ federated SQL queries, and multimodal NVIDIA Nemotron legal adjudication.
